title: Rivet ingest mediator and contract sleuth
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The Console telemetry pipeline is experiencing intermittent event rejections and silent schema drift for new SDK releases. Current rigid validators cause customer-visible errors or require manual schema onboarding. Goal: Build a resilient ingest mediator (Rivet) that acts as an intelligent gateway between the public telemetry onramp and downstream transforms. Rivet performs progressive contract analysis, automated soft-coercion of minor schema drift, and a sleuthing mode that classifies incoming unknown event shapes for rapid onboarding and alerting. This ticket covers design, initial implementation, and a canary rollout for a single SDK family.
background: We currently run a hard-schema validator in the ingress path that returns 4xx for shape mismatches. This protects downstream logic but results in false positives for minor field additions and leads to support tickets. Recent incidents: SDK v2.8 beta added optional metadata and triggered a 12% rejection spike on the ingest gateway (incident IN-2025-01-30). The telemetry team wants a more nuanced approach: maintain contract guarantees for critical fields while allowing evolutionary changes for non-critical fields.
goals: Reduce customer-visible telemetry rejects from 12% to <1% for minor non-breaking changes
Provide signal (dashboards/alerts) for meaningful schema drift within 30m
Enable per-customer validation profiles (strict vs permissive)
Keep downstream consumption contracts intact for critical fields (customer_id, event_type, timestamp)
acceptance_criteria: Rivet proxy deployed in front of current ingress with feature flag off by default
Rivet automatically soft-coerces added optional fields and routes accepted events to existing pipeline
A sleuth classification table and dashboard emitted to Console Telemetry with schema fingerprint and change risk score
Per-customer profile toggles honored (from Console Config service) and cover both strict and permissive modes
End-to-end test demonstrating no regression in downstream consumers (replay test and contract checks)
design_decisions: Place Rivet as a thin, horizontally scalable proxy in the edge tier to avoid touching existing consumers
Use a two-stage validation: quick structural check for critical keys, then async classification for unknown shapes
Soft-coercion ruleset: allow unknown fields, coerce numeric strings to numbers when unambiguous, normalize timestamp formats, but reject if critical key missing
Maintain a per-customer schema profile keyed by account id. Profiles pulled from Console Config cache with TTL and fallback to global default
Emit a change-alert event to telemetry-alerts topic whenever new schema fingerprint crosses risk threshold (>=0.7)
implementation_notes: New service: rivet-ingest-proxy (Go). Uses existing ingress auth middleware and reuses current ingress rate limiter
Schema engine: incremental fingerprinting using Murmur3 of sorted keys + heuristic typing; classifier uses lightweight decision tree model stored as a JSON ruleset for explainability
Storage: latest known schema per-account in Redis (compact), historical samples in telemetry-raw-bucket for offline analysis
Backpressure: if classification queue grows > 90% capacity, switch to permissive passthrough mode for affected accounts and emit incident metric
Feature-flag gating via LaunchDarkly key: rivet.ingest.enable, with rollout targeting internal test accounts first
testing_plan: Unit tests for coercion rules and fingerprint collisions
Integration: replay suite using historical event dump (2025-01) to validate acceptance rate improvements
Chaos test: simulate classifier lag and verify backpressure fallback toggles permissive mode without dropping events
Canary: route 1% of traffic from SDK family A through Rivet for 48 hours with detailed metrics and alerting
Contract tests: downstream consumer mocks must pass on events after Rivet processing
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dev deployment + automated tests (complete)
Phase 1: Internal canary (engineering accounts) via feature flag for 24-48h
Phase 2: Public canary for SDK family A (1% traffic) with active SRE monitoring
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% per-customer toggle, validate metrics at each step
Rollback: feature flag off + drain in-flight classification queue; postmortem if rejects increase
metrics: ingest.reject_rate: target <1% for non-critical schema changes
schema-drift-alerts: number of alerts per 24h (target: informative, not spam)
events-processed-per-second: throughput target matches current ingress capacity
fallback-activations: count of permissive fallbacks triggered
dependencies: Console Config service - profile API for per-customer validation settings
Telemetry-alerts pipeline - to receive schema risk alerts
SRE runbook updates for new fallback behavior
